title: Add-ons
body_markdown:
### New
- **Add-ons, for installs without Pro.** One feature each, one payment that covers 2 years, no subscription, up to three homes. PadSpan Pro includes them all. They share one key, entered in Settings → Features → PadSpan licence like any other; the card lists each add-on with its date.
  - **Audio** ($6.45 CAD): volume, mute and off for each room's players in the room's card, and a speaker beside a playing room's name.
  - **Alarm & security** ($6.45): Arm and Disarm in the emergency button, the emergency lights test (the button, its list and Force off), the door, garage and gate card on the map, marking openers in Devices → Door Openers, building an opener or a lock from relays, and linking an opener or a lock to a door in the Atlas builder.
  - **Wi-Fi coverage** ($6.45): the Wi-Fi coverage tab.
  - **Climate map** ($8.65): the ♨ Heatmap on the Atlas.
  - **Time travel** ($7.55): Full house activity, the day replayed on the Atlas.
  - **Vacation Mode & presets** ($4.25): Vacation Mode and the Whole house presets.
  - **Looks pack** ($4.25): the Graphite, Ocean, Dusk and Day themes, and on the Atlas Showcase with its themes, the West Coast Forest and the Look presets.
  - **Forensics** ($5.56): Forensics recording.
  - **Presence insights** ($5.56): Busy Times and Locate.
- **Coming with the free 3D house: Advanced map creation** ($8.65 CAD), not on sale yet: AI plan reading (the Plans tool, Line up plans, Rooms from plans and Let Claude draw your rooms), reading a photo, a LiDAR scan's doors, windows, furniture and stairs in the 3D house, Furniture from scans, and floor plans from a LiDAR scan. PadSpan Pro includes it. Until it is on sale nothing changes for anyone: the first of these stay PadSpan Pro's, and a floor plan from a LiDAR scan stays free.
- **Audio on the classic layout.** Settings → Atlas → Audio, off by default, does for the whole house what the ⋯ list's Audio line does per screen on the new layout: a speaker beside a playing room's name, and Audio in the room's card with Match rooms for an administrator. It shows where Audio is allowed.

### Changed
- **The emergency lights test moved into Alarm & security.** It was free; it now needs PadSpan Pro or the Alarm & security add-on, and Home Assistant refuses its test, Force off and switches without either. A test already running always shows, and can be ended or forced off. Still free on every install: an alarm going off, shown in the button with nothing to press, the red emergency banner for a leak, smoke, CO, gas or an alarm, locking and unlocking on the map and in the room card, and Alert pulse.
- **Each paid feature asks for its own add-on.** Where a feature was PadSpan Pro's alone, it now says "PadSpan Pro or the … add-on", with the add-on's price. A Bright Pro key keeps everything it had.
- **Full house activity draws what the install may show.** Replayed on the Atlas, placed lights and Showcase need what they need on the Atlas itself, so Time travel alone replays the free map.
- **The licence card names an add-on key as such.** It never calls it Pro, and offers the add-ons in one list beside Pro to an install without Pro. An install with an add-on key can still start the Pro trial: its key is kept aside and comes back by itself when the trial ends, after its 14 days' grace; a trial bought in place keeps its paid key. Every licence check now says which add-ons this PadSpan knows, so the licence server answers an add-on key only to a PadSpan that can tell it from Pro.

title: Audio: the volume counts as Control4 does; matches are kept as you pick them
body_markdown:
### Fixed
- **− and + on an Audio player no longer count in tens.** A Control4 room moves 1 step in 100 a press, but the card showed a guessed level 10 higher or lower straight away, and drawing that guess again under your finger could lose the next quick press. A player that steps itself (Control4 and the other whole-house systems) now shows only the level it reports, so every press lands. A player Home Assistant steps for it (one that can only be set to a level) still shows its next level at once.
- **The Audio matching card keeps every pick as you make it.** A room picked, ▲ or ▼, or Include Home Assistant speakers is saved at once, and the card's own guesses are kept as it opens, so nothing is lost by closing it. Save and Cancel are gone: **Done** closes the card, and a line beside it says Saved (or Not saved, with the reason, if Home Assistant refused).

title: Audio: its own name, and its setup in the ⋯ list
body_markdown:
### New
- **Set up › on the Audio line.** The ⋯ list's **Audio** line has a **Set up ›** that opens the matching card (which player is in which room, **Match Control4 to HA** in a Control4 house) right there over the map, ticked or not, in the flat map's list and the 3D view's, on a wall screen too. It is an administrator's, as the matching always was.
- **The speaker by a room's name, in 3D too.** With **Audio** ticked, the 3D view now shows the same small speaker the flat map does at a room's name while one of its players is on, struck through while the room's first player is muted, and nothing while they are all off. Where the names are hidden it stands where the name would be. A tap on it opens the room's panel, with its Audio; a tap on the map never switches anything.

### Changed
- **Room controls are called Audio.** The line in the Atlas map's ⋯ (Show on this screen) now says **Audio**, in the flat map's list and the 3D view's. What it does is the same, and a screen that had it ticked keeps its tick.

### Fixed
- **A player's buttons stay on one line.** In the 3D view's room panel on a wall screen, a player's **Mute**, **−**, level, **+** and ⏻ wrapped onto two lines. They now stay together on one line, under the player's name where the panel is narrow.

title: Room controls on the Atlas
body_markdown:
### New
- **Room controls: a room's music, shades and thermostat in its sheet.** Tick **Room controls** in the Atlas map's ⋯ (per screen, off unless ticked). A room's sheet then shows its temperature, humidity and who is there, a **Room off** button for its lights and players, an **Audio** part with each player's mute, volume − and +, level and off, one **Shades** row (open, stop, close all of them) and each thermostat's setpoint with − and +. Every press is one call to Home Assistant; anyone who can switch the lights can use them, wall screens too. Off, the map and the sheets are exactly as before.
- **A speaker beside a room's name while a player there is on.** With room controls on, a small speaker shows beside the name of a room whose player is on, struck through while the room's first player is muted, and nothing while they are all off. A tap on it opens the room's sheet.
- **Match players to rooms, Control4 and the other whole-house systems.** Control4, Crestron, Savant, Russound, Nuvo, Monoprice, Xantech, Triad, Denon, Yamaha and Anthem players are recognised by their Home Assistant integration. An administrator matches them to the map's rooms once (**Match rooms**, or **Match Control4 to HA** in a Control4 house), with first guesses from each player's area or name. Two players can share a room, a Control4 zone and a Denon zone say, in the order you set. **Include Home Assistant speakers** (off unless ticked) adds Music Assistant, ESPHome, Cast and TV players.

title: Floors and walls in Furnish; Lights follow people; Plans from Easy Floorplan, DXF and Floorplanner; Share a replay; Walk through the 3D house; Yesterday at home
body_markdown:
0.38.295 was never published (a check failed); everything it held is here.

### New
- **Floors and wall colours for each room (Live Aboard, Furnish).** In Mapping → Furnish, tap a room's floor: pick its floor (wood, light wood, tile, stone, carpet or concrete, each drawn with its own colour and planks or joints), the colour of its walls inside, one wall in a colour of its own, and the colour of the floor's outside walls. Each is one Undo and kept at Save, in Live Aboard's own file, so a PadSpan backup carries it and a restore brings it back. They show in the Classic and Studio looks; a Showcase theme and the Atlas's look keep their own colours. Nothing changes until you pick something. With the usage report on, it counts which floor material was picked and that walls were coloured, never which room or colour.
- **Lights follow people (free, off until you turn it on).** PadSpan can switch room lights itself: a room's lights go on when someone with a named phone, watch or tag comes in, and off once nobody has been in it for the time you set (2 minutes unless you choose 30 seconds to an hour). Turn it on in Settings → Tracking → Home Assistant and integrations → Lights follow people, then add your rooms. Until you do, nothing changes.
- **Per room**: which lights (a new room starts with its Home Assistant area's lights), the off delay, only when dark (the sun down, or a light sensor below a level you set), and quiet hours in which nothing turns on.
- **It never fights a light switch.** A light someone turns off by hand while they are in the room stays off until everyone has left the room for a minute and someone comes back. A light turned on in a room nobody tracked has been in is never turned off.
- **No waiting for the room change.** A room change waits for Room Change Delay, so the light would come on late. Give a room its motion or occupancy sensor and the lights go on as soon as PadSpan's latest reading puts someone in that room and the sensor sees them.
- **Per person**: everyone you have named counts, except guest tags. Untick anyone (or a tag that stays put, like keys) who shouldn't switch lights, or tick a guest tag to let it.
- **Three Home Assistant blueprints** for people who prefer their own automations: room lights follow people, lights on in whichever room you walk into, and lights off when a room is empty. Import links are in the manual, chapter 14.
- **The opt-in usage report counts it**: lights turned on and off, a light left off because it was turned off by hand, an entry in quiet hours or daylight, an entry a sensor sped up, a light that didn't answer. Counts only, never a room, a name or a light.
- **Import a plan from another app.** Mapping → Upload → **No floor plan? Ways to get one** has a new way, second on the list: pick an Easy Floorplan card's YAML, a DXF drawing (saved as text) or a Floorplanner export (the `.fml`, or the zip it comes in), and PadSpan draws that floor to scale, the way it draws a phone's room scan. Easy Floorplan brings its walls, doors, windows and rooms, and a room linked to a Home Assistant area is named after it; a DXF's closed polylines become rooms, named by the text inside them, with the unit from the drawing; Floorplanner brings its walls, doors, windows and rooms in centimetres. A file with no unit asks for the drawing's width (an Easy Floorplan drawing without one is scaled from its doors, and says so), and a file with several floors asks which one. The file's rooms are outlines, not new rooms: choose each Home Assistant room and press **Use the outline the file gives** it. Whatever isn't used (devices and their entities, furniture, texts, curves drawn straight) is listed, in the message and beside the rooms on the plan. Free, like every way to a plan.
- **Share a replay: a short clip of people moving through your house, ready to post.** In Traceback's playback, pick the stretch (ten minutes to a few hours works best) and press **Share a replay**. PadSpan turns it into a 10 to 30 second clip on the floor stack Traceback plays on. The clip starts where the first person changes room and plays still stretches fast, so it leads with people moving, not with the house.
- **Privacy is the point.** Names become **Person 1**, **Person 2** (or initials); device names, addresses and signal readings are left out; room names stay as they are or become generic ones (**Bedroom**, **Room 3**); floors are numbered, never named; only the time of day shows, never the date. The clip is drawn from your rooms' outlines, so no plan image, address or coordinates are in it. Before you save, the dialog plays the clip as it will be saved and lists what it hides, with each name and room as the clip shows it.
- **Wide or vertical, MP4, WebM or GIF.** MP4 where the browser can record it (Chrome and Edge can), saved as a plain MP4 at a steady 30 frames a second; WebM where it can't (Firefox); a GIF in any browser. A small **made with PadSpan** mark sits in a corner; untick it to leave it out. The clip is made in your browser and saved to your computer: PadSpan uploads nothing. Free in every edition. The 3D house comes later.
- **In the opt-in report:** the dialog opened, a clip saved by format and shape, initials or Person N, room names kept, the mark switched off, a clip that failed. Counts only, never a name, a room or the clip.
- **Walk through your house in Live Aboard.** **Walk** (bottom right; on a narrow screen in **View ▾**) puts you in the house at eye height, just inside the front door or in the room you have open. Walk with **W A S D** or **↑ ↓** (**← →** turn, **Shift** to hurry), or with the stick that shows on a touch screen; drag to look round. Walls, railings, window sills and closed doors stop you, a door opens when its sensor says so, and stairs take you to the floor above and back down. **✕ Stop walking** or **Esc** puts the 3D view back exactly as it was. Standing still, nothing is drawn, so a slow tablet stays cool. Live Aboard is still experimental: tell us where it lets you through a wall or stops you on a stair.
- **The usage report counts walks (only if you send it).** A walk started, and whether it used the keys, the stick, a drag or the stairs. Never where, which room or how far.
- **Yesterday at home: one short message each morning about the day before.** Off until you turn it on in Settings → Tracking → Phones and guest tags. At the time you choose it tells, through a Home Assistant notify target or a Home Assistant notification, who came and went and when, guest tags that arrived or left, the rooms empty longest, and lights left on in rooms where nobody was; you tick which of these it includes. The figures are Traceback's for that day, and the message links to Traceback on that day. A quiet day gets "Nothing to report", never an empty message, and a restart never sends a day twice. Free in every edition.

title: Your house alarm inside the emergency button; German leftovers on Rooms and Traceback; Wi-Fi while the robot cleans; Start with a rough house from your Home Assistant rooms
body_markdown:
### New
- **Your house alarm, inside the Atlas's emergency button (PadSpan Bright and Pro).** If Home Assistant has an alarm panel (Alarmo, or your alarm system's own integration), the round emergency button at the top right of the Atlas now holds it. Its centre is the alarm's shield, in the alarm's colour: grey disarmed, blue armed, amber pending, red and pulsing while it goes off. Press the button for its card: the alarm on top, with Arm home, Arm away, Arm night and the rest (only the modes your alarm supports) or Disarm, and your emergency lights below. Every arm and disarm asks first, and asks for the code when the alarm wants one; PadSpan never keeps the code. A wrong code is refused by Home Assistant, and PadSpan says so in Home Assistant's own words. It works on wall screens and for every household member who can use the alarm in Home Assistant, as unlocking a door does.
- **The button changes with what your house has.** Emergency lights and no alarm: the red emergency lighting button exactly as before. An alarm and no emergency lights: the alarm's own button, a plain ring around the shield. Both: the red emergency ring with the alarm's shield as its centre; the lighting test then starts from **Start test** in the card, so a hand going for the alarm never starts it. Neither: no button.
- **An alarm going off shows in the red emergency banner, on every screen and every edition.** The same banner a leak, smoke, gas or CO alarm raises, naming what set it off when the alarm says (Alarmo does): "Alarm going off: House · Back door". On the free edition the button shows the alarm only while it is going off, and its card says so with nothing to press.
- **The opt-in usage report counts it**: the alarm's controls shown, an arm, a disarm, one Home Assistant refused. Counts only, never a code or which alarm.
- **The robot vacuum can collect Wi-Fi while it cleans.** A new switch on the robot's card, **Collect Wi-Fi while it cleans**, off until you turn it on. While the robot is cleaning or driving on its own and its live position is on, PadSpan reads the robot's Wi-Fi signal and where it is about every 5 seconds. It only reads, never tells the robot to do anything, and reads nothing while the robot is docked or on a room location run. Readings taken on the move count a tenth of the ones from a run's stops, and the last 5,000 are kept separately, so they never push a stop's reading out. On the Wi-Fi coverage screen they show as faint squares under the robot's diamonds, and **While it cleaned** hides them. Other integrations reading the robot's Wi-Fi now get each reading's kind (stop or moving) and weight.
- **A first map with no drawing at all.** While no room is drawn yet, Setup (at the top) and Mapping's empty Library offer **Start with a rough house from your Home Assistant rooms**. **Show what it will make** lists each floor with its rooms, and what it leaves out and why; **Make the rough house** then puts one square box for each Home Assistant area on its floor, named as the area, on a blank floor marked "rough start" for each floor that has no plan yet. A box is 3.5 m across, a little bigger for an area with many devices. Your devices show in their rooms straight away. An area with no floor in Home Assistant goes on the floor you pick. It only runs when you press it, it is free, and it never touches calibration, receivers or walls, or a room or plan you already have; a second press makes nothing.
- **The boxes are a starting point.** The rough plan's note says how many rooms are still boxes and offers **Reshape the rooms** (Mapping → Layout in Advanced; in Basic the Setup Wizard's rooms step, with the boxes drawn dashed) and **Upload a plan of this floor**. A room you trace, on the rough plan or on a real plan uploaded later, and put on the map with **Put it on the map** takes the place of its box under the same name, so it keeps its Home Assistant area. A box you have reshaped is yours and is never replaced. Until then the boxes never get in the way of a real plan: Setup's Draw the rooms step stays to do, the real plan opens on its Rooms tool, and Let Claude draw your rooms is still offered for it.
- **In the opt-in report:** whether the rough house was offered, previewed and made (with how many rooms, as a band), and which way on was taken afterwards. Words and counts only.

### Fixed
- **Rooms in German: "Art des Raums" no longer covers "Empfänger ansehen".** The kind-of-space list was as wide as its longest choice, and in German that choice ran over the Receivers field beside it. The list now stays inside its own column (the outdoor surface list too), on a wide screen and a phone.
- **Traceback speaks German everywhere.** "No traceback frames loaded", the empty-range and load-failure messages, the 5/15/30 min buttons, "to" between the dates, the minutes box, the Insights and Busy Times buttons and the Vacation Mode tooltip were still in English with German loaded.

title: Pro for life ends December 15; Lighter rain
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **Pro for life ends December 15.** It's $89 until November 30, then $168 until December 15. After that there's no lifetime. From then PadSpan Pro is $85 for two years or $49 a year, and every new PadSpan feature is included while it runs. Lifetime keys already sold stay lifetime.
- **One card on Overview says so, once:** "Pro for life ends Dec 15", for administrators, until December 15. It replaces the November 30 card, so if you saw that one you'll see this one once too. No thanks takes it away.
- **From December 16, every price in PadSpan switches by itself:** the licence card, the trial card and the paywalls show $49 a year and $85 for two years. PadSpan Bright Pro is no longer sold; in PadSpan Bright the buy button offers PadSpan Pro, whose key unlocks light placement there too. New testers get one year of Pro instead of two. Keys already issued keep their terms.
- **Rain is more see-through.** On the flat Atlas and in the 3D house, rain is drawn at a little over half its old strength, so it reads as rain falling past the house, not as a white snow-like veil. Snow is as it was.

title: Fit keeps Edgecut; A PDF plan, in the manual; The robot's Wi-Fi on the Wi-Fi coverage map; The robot vacuum's card, and room location runs; The usage report says how long one screen shows PadSpan
body_markdown:
### New
- **The robot vacuum's Wi-Fi on the Wi-Fi coverage map.** With UniFi Utopia's Wi-Fi survey (still a test build), the Wi-Fi readings the robot takes on its room location runs show on the Wi-Fi coverage screen as their own layer, "Robot (floor level, 2.4 GHz)": a small diamond at each spot where it stood, coloured by the signal the robot itself heard. Point at one to see that signal, the access point it was on, how strongly that access point heard the robot (when UniFi saw it within 45 seconds of the middle of its stop), and when. The readings are taken about 10 cm off the floor, so they read weaker than at hand height; they are kept apart from the phones' and devices' colours and from What to fix. The layer is there only when there are readings, on to start with, and turning it off is remembered in that browser.
- **Other integrations can read the robot's Wi-Fi directly.** For integrations in the same Home Assistant, the readings the `padspan_ha/robot_wifi_readings` command gives are also available without the websocket (`vacuum_run.robot_wifi_snapshot`). UniFi Utopia uses it.
- **The robot vacuum has its own card.** With a Valetudo robot linked, press and hold the robot on the Atlas or in the 3D house to open it. It talks to the robot's own Valetudo (no vacuum entity or MQTT needed): what the robot is doing, its battery, and Start, Pause and Dock. If Valetudo's login is on, the card asks for its user and password and says so plainly when the robot answers 401. For administrators; a tap on the robot still shows its small card.
- **You choose how the robot's points are used.** Before the first run the card asks: count them like your own, fill gaps and count them less (only in rooms where you have fewer than 3 points of your own, at half weight), or use them for Find mistakes and Wi-Fi only. Nothing is picked for you. Change it any time; the card says what that would change for earlier runs and lets you apply it in one undoable step, or leave them. After each run it shows how your own test spots scored before and after.
- **Room location runs (optional, off until you start one).** Stick a fixed-address Bluetooth beacon (iBeacon or Eddystone, not an AirTag or a Tile) on top of the robot, and the card's Room location part sends the robot to spots about 1.5 m apart in every room (or just one), clear of the walls. At each spot it stands still for about 20 seconds while PadSpan listens to the beacon, and the spot is added to calibration. Calibration is backed up before every run, Stop sends the robot back to its dock, and Undo takes out exactly the points one run added, never your own; every run whose points are still there keeps its own Undo. If the robot heads home on its own or its battery drops below 20 %, the run ends there (and below 20 % none starts). The card shows what is missing first: the robot's address, its map from Valetudo, and whether the beacon is heard right now. On a wall screen it shows the robot's state only.
- **Find mistakes.** A button on the robot's card opens a card of its own that lists receivers placed in the wrong spot or on the wrong floor, worked out from the points the runs already collected (no extra driving): which receiver, where it is placed, where the readings put it, how sure, and a link to its placement. A receiver is judged only from spots lying round it; the others are listed as not enough readings. Nothing is moved.
- **The robot's Wi-Fi at each spot.** During a run the robot also reports its Wi-Fi signal at each spot; PadSpan keeps the last 2,000 for the Wi-Fi coverage map, and other integrations can read them. A spot where the Wi-Fi can't be read is not skipped.
- **Runs listen harder and stop cleanly.** At each stop PadSpan counts every packet each receiver hears from the beacon (Home Assistant 2026.10 and newer; older versions read each receiver once a second), drops a stop the robot moved during, skips a spot the robot can't reach, takes a stop where the robot settles close to its target, keeps clear of your no-go areas, virtual walls and obstacles, and ends a run sending nothing more when someone or a Valetudo timer takes the robot over. A run won't start if the robot's map has changed since it was imported, and the card says when a Valetudo timer is due within two hours. Find mistakes now calls a receiver "on the wrong floor" when it hears the robot about as strongly as the receivers on the robot's own floor do.

### Changed
- **The manual, the README and the floor-plans guide say a plan can be a PDF.** Mapping → Upload has taken a PDF since 0.38.287: a plan with several pages asks which page to use, and that page is drawn as a picture in your browser. The manual's upload step (English and German) now says so, and what to do with a password-protected PDF.
- **The robot is always on the map while its link is on.** With Robot Vacuum Import on, the robot is drawn on the Atlas and in the 3D house whether people and tags are shown or not, so its card is always one hold away.
- **The robot's points are PadSpan's, not yours.** In every count that tells your own calibration points from automatic ones, the robot's points count as automatic. The beacons' own clean-ups never remove them; only a run's Undo does.
- **The opt-in usage report says how much of the day your busiest screen showed PadSpan.** With the report on, Home Assistant adds up the minutes each screen showed a PadSpan page, and the report says only the busiest single screen's minutes, over the whole day and from 7 am to 11 pm in your Home Assistant's time zone, next to how many minutes the report covers. It never says which screen: each browser's random screen ID stays in your Home Assistant, kept until the report goes (so a restart doesn't lose the count) and then forgotten. Before, the minutes of all your screens were added together, so one wall screen on all day looked the same as three screens on for a third of it. Preview shows it as `top_screen`.

### Fixed
- **Fit and 100% no longer forget Edgecut.** With Edgecut ticked, moving the map and pressing Fit (or 100%) went back to the whole house as if Edgecut were off. Now it goes back to Edgecut's own framing, centred. In the 3D house, Iso, Top and ⟳ 90° keep Edgecut on too and frame it from the new angle; only Whole house or a saved view turns it off.

title: Edgecut: the rooms fill the screen
body_markdown:
### New
- **Edgecut.** A new line in the Atlas's ⋯ list (and in the 3D house's Views ▾), off unless a screen ticks it: the map zooms in until the rooms fill the screen edge to edge, with no empty ground beside the house. The house runs off the screen the other way: its outer edges, and on a stack of floors the top and bottom floors, are cut. It works on the flat map and in the 3D house, keeps the 3D camera's angle, and frames again when the screen changes size or another floor is chosen. Drag to another part of the house and it stays there; zoom by hand and your zoom wins until you go back to 100% (the flat map) or the camera's idle return (the 3D house). Each screen keeps its own choice: tick it on the wall and the laptop stays as it was.

title: Rooms, Traceback, the Atlas and Live Aboard in German
body_markdown:
### New
- **Rooms, Traceback, the Atlas and Live Aboard speak German.** With your Home Assistant profile set to German: the Rooms page; Traceback with Playback, New Objects, Insights, Busy Times and the distance table; the Atlas (the map's controls, room and floor sheets, the control card, the door and lock card, emergency lighting, Vacation Mode's options, presets, the light index, the heights list and the scene row); Live Aboard's bar, menus, cards, the Show on this screen list and People & devices; and Edit and Furnish with Strip, From a photo, Import and every piece of furniture's name and settings.
- **The Atlas page loads its own language.** Opened from the sidebar or on a wall screen, it was English whatever your profile said, the Hide HA button included. It now follows your profile like the rest of PadSpan.

### Changed
- French and Dutch stay English on these screens for now.
- Still English in German: Edit → Plans, the shared furniture library, Set up Live Aboard, the power team card, the wall screens card, Showcase theme and Automorph style names, furniture option words (slim, rolled, queen), door type names, and a few single words whose English means two things (the index columns Light and Health, a door's state Open, and Top, Shade, Main, Bath, Build, Share and Tag in Furnish).

title: The help and docs say what PadSpan does; The usage report fits a big house again
body_markdown:
### Changed
- **The 3D house's descriptions say "turn, pan and zoom".** Settings, the help and the Atlas's tooltip said you could walk around the house; the 3D view turns, pans and zooms.
- **The weather tip names Bright Pro too.** The moving rain and snow on the Atlas come with Bright Pro as well as PadSpan Pro, and Settings and the help now say so.
- **The Live Aboard wizard's tip says PadSpan Pro.** It said the 3D house also came with Bright Pro, which it does not.
- **The README, the manual and the website's guides were checked against the product.** A lock opens its card on a tap and asks before unlocking; alerts go through Home Assistant's notify services; the floor-plans guide lists the iPhone or iPad scan and the blank floor; the manual's Atlas chapter covers blind and garage openers, the scene row and the heatmap; the install steps match the release zip.

### Fixed
- **A big house's usage report goes again.** The opt-in report had a hard cap of 8 KB, and a house that uses a lot of PadSpan outgrew it: first screen and tool counts were dropped to make it fit, then the whole report was refused, every day. The cap is now 32 KB, in PadSpan and on the server that receives it. Most reports are about 7 KB.

title: Access points are placed in Mapping
body_markdown:
### New
- **Wi-Fi access points on the Atlas.** With UniFi Utopia, each access point is a Home Assistant device, and Mapping places it like any other device: it has its own symbol and the "Wi-Fi" filter. The Wi-Fi coverage screen draws each one where it is placed (until then dashed, where the devices that hear it best suggest), and "Place in Mapping" opens Mapping with that access point selected.

### Changed
- **Wi-Fi coverage no longer drags access points.** One place to put them: Mapping.
- **The note under far-access-point findings** says devices differ in their transmitters and antennas, not only antennas.

title: A fairer accuracy score; PDF floor plans
body_markdown:
### New
- **PDF floor plans in Mapping → Upload.** Pick a PDF the way you pick a picture. PadSpan draws the page in your browser, and the upload goes on as for any image, with the same crop, size and scale steps. When a PDF has several pages, you choose the one with the plan. Drawn plans (an architect's or a builder's export) stay sharp because the page is drawn, not photographed. Black-and-white scans from an office scanner or a permit office work too. A password-protected or broken PDF says so. Nothing extra loads unless you pick a PDF.

### Fixed
- **Calibration's "How accurate it is now" counts only what it can test.** Four changes to how the score is worked out:
  - A room calibrated at one spot only is listed as not counted. It used to count as wrong, because the test holds out the spot and its neighbours and nothing of that room was left.
  - A spot's true room is the room drawn where it stands, not a label that disagrees with it. How many disagree is shown.
  - Spots heard by a single receiver are left out, as live tracking leaves them out.
  - In a big calibration, each room is tested in proportion to its spots.
  On a real house the score went from 4 % to 29 % rooms right for fingerprints, and from 12 % to 28 % for spatial, on the same data.
  Nothing about how positions are worked out changed. If you turned on "pick the better method", the comparison it makes now uses this fairer score. The opt-in report counts how many rooms couldn't be tested (a number, never a name).

title: Wi-Fi coverage says what to fix
body_markdown:
### New
- **Wi-Fi coverage (test): what to fix, first.** Above the map, UniFi Utopia's findings, most urgent first, each with what to do: placed devices that keep dropping off Wi-Fi, that sit on a far access point while a neighbour a few metres away hears another one much better, that are very weak, PadSpan receivers on weak Wi-Fi (their reports arrive late or not at all), rooms where a phone spends time on weak Wi-Fi, and before and after for a device that moved to another access point. A click shows the finding on the plan.
- **Access points on the plan.** Each access point is drawn where you put it, or (dashed) where the devices that hear it best suggest. An administrator drags one to where it really is, or sets its floor under "Where the access points are".

### Changed
- **UniFi Blocker is now UniFi Utopia.** The Wi-Fi coverage tab asks UniFi Utopia (`unifi_utopia/...`) and names it.
